clusters.name: Intrusion (ASD)
items: Involuntary distressing memories
Traumatic dreams
Dissociative reactions (Flashbacks / trauma play reenactment)
Psychological or physiological distress at cues

clusters.name: Negative Mood (ASD)
items: Persistent inability to experience positive emotions

clusters.name: Dissociation (ASD)
items: Altered sense of reality (depersonalization / derealization)
Dissociative amnesia for key trauma details

clusters.name: Avoidance (ASD)
items: Avoidance of internal distressing memories or thoughts
Avoidance of external reminders (people, places, activities)

clusters.name: Arousal (ASD)
items: Sleep disturbance
Irritable behavior and angry outbursts
Hypervigilance
Concentration problems
Exaggerated startle response

clusters.name: Adjustment Disorder Core
items: Emotional or behavioral symptoms in response to an identifiable stressor
Disproportionate distress or significant functional impairment

criteria.thresholds: ASD: >=9/14 symptoms across 5 categories, duration 3 days to 1 month. Adjustment: onset within 3 months of stressor, resolves within 6 months after stressor ends (unless chronic).
subtypes: With mixed anxiety and depressed mood (F43.23)
With mixed disturbance of emotions and conduct (F43.25)
Persistent / Chronic (>=6 months with ongoing stressor)

epidemiology.prevalence: ASD: <20% non-interpersonal trauma, 19-50% interpersonal assault. Adjustment: <1% community, 2.94% primary care, 11-50% hospital consultation-liaison.
epidemiology.onset_age_typical: All ages (ASD onset within 3 days post-trauma; Adjustment onset within 3 months of stressor)
epidemiology.prognosis: ASD: ~50% remit within 1 month, ~50% transition to PTSD. Adjustment: generally favorable, most resolve within 3-6 months.

etiology.genetic: Elevated baseline acoustic startle reactivity and autonomic responsiveness increase risk.
etiology.neurobiology: Amygdala hyperactivity (Fear circuit), HPA axis hyperactivation (Cortisol), Locus Coeruleus hyperresponsiveness (NE), impaired top-down PFC/hippocampal inhibition.
etiology.environmental: Interpersonal trauma, severe acute life stressors, lack of social support, childhood adversity (ACEs).

first_line: TF-CBT (PRACTICE model: Psychoeducation, Relaxation, Affective regulation, Cognitive coping, Trauma narrative, In vivo exposure, Conjoint parent-child, Enhancing safety)
Crisis Intervention and Supportive Case Management (Adjustment Disorder)
second_line: Prazosin (alpha-1 adrenergic antagonist for trauma nightmares and nocturnal hyperarousal)
SSRIs (Fluoxetine, Escitalopram) for persistent comorbid anxiety/depression
Morphine (acute hospital administration post-trauma to block memory consolidation)
D-Cycloserine (NMDA partial agonist to enhance fear extinction during exposure)
key_side_effects: SSRIs: antidepressant-induced activation, agitation, suicidal ideation risk in pediatric population
treatment.monitoring: Monitor suicidal behavior, activation symptoms, blood pressure (Prazosin), and symptom duration at 1 month (ASD to PTSD transition) and 6 months (Adjustment resolution).

items: UCLA PTSD Reaction Index for DSM-5
CPSS-5 (Child PTSD Symptom Scale for DSM-5)
PsySTART rapid triage tool (13 questions)
PAPA (Preschool Age Psychiatric Assessment)
K-SADS-PL semi-structured interview
key_numbers: 3 months onset limit for Adjustment Disorder
1 month cutoff for ASD to PTSD transition

items: Mild Traumatic Brain Injury / TBI (postconcussive headache, dizziness, light sensitivity)
Hyperthyroidism (hyperarousal, agitation, tachycardia)
Complex Partial Epilepsy (flashback and dissociative mimics)
Substance Intoxication or Withdrawal (stimulants, alcohol, cannabis)
PANS / PANDAS (acute onset behavioral dysregulation and severe anxiety)
key_numbers: 3 days minimum symptom duration to diagnose ASD vs normal transient stress response
1 month maximum duration for ASD before re-evaluating for TBI vs PTSD

high_yield: ASD duration must be 3 days to 1 month post-trauma; if symptoms persist beyond 1 month, change diagnosis to PTSD.
ASD requires at least 9 of 14 symptoms from any of the 5 categories (Intrusion, Negative Mood, Dissociation, Avoidance, Arousal).
Adjustment Disorder requires symptom onset within 3 months of an identifiable stressor and resolution within 6 months after the stressor or its consequences terminate.
Adjustment Disorder with disturbance of conduct (F43.24) is common in adolescents and is strongly associated with elevated suicide risk.
Fear extinction is mediated by VMPFC/hippocampal activation of GABAergic interneurons in the Intercalated Cell Mass (ITC) of the Amygdala.
Prazosin acts as an alpha-1 adrenergic antagonist in the Amygdala to reduce traumatic nightmares and nocturnal hyperarousal.
